name: Question 3
problem:
Find the solution of the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.2p+0.3q=0.6 \\ 0.2p-0.1q=0.4\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $10,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.2p+0.3q=0.6 & |\times 10 \\ 0.2p-0.1q=0.4 & |\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2p+3q=6 \\ 2p-q=4\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the second equation by $-1,$ then we will get a $-2p$ term that can cancel with the $2p$ term in the first equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2p+3q=6 &  \\ 2p-q=4 & |\,\times (-1)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2p+3q=6 \\ -2p+q=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $p$-variable and allows us to solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{2p}+3q & =6 \\ -\cancel{2p}+q & =-4 \\ (3q+q) & =(6-4) \\ 4q & =2 \\ q & =\frac{2}{4} \\ q & =0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $q=0.5$ into the equation $2p-q=4$ to solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2p-q & =4 \\ 2p-0.5 & =4 \\ 2p & =4.5 \\ p & =\frac{4.5}{2} \\ p & =2.25\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $p=2.25,\,q=0.5.$

EXPLANATION

To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by 10, as follows:

{0.2p+0.3q=0.6|×100.2p−0.1q=0.4|×10⟹{2p+3q=62p−q=4

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the second equation by −1, then we will get a −2p term that can cancel with the 2p term in the first equation:

{2p+3q=62p−q=4|×(−1)⟹{2p+3q=6−2p+q=−4

Adding the two equations eliminates the p-variable and allows us to solve for q:

2p+3q=6−2p+q=−4(3q+q)=(6−4)4q=2q=24q=0.5

Finally, we can substitute q=0.5 into the equation 2p−q=4 to solve for p:

2p−q=42p−0.5=42p=4.5p=4.52p=2.25

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is p=2.25,q=0.5.
